decisions.note: Rejects truncated gzip archives before restore.

atApproval.title: Tidy history table

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Improvements were made to the interface, including clearer history and target tables, new sidebar shell with theme support and custom font, improved status badges, interactive progress on submit buttons, inline error rendering, and expanded detail on backup and restore statuses.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: These changes enhance usability, readability, and feedback within the user console, resolving confusion and an unfinished appearance.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: Table formatting was updated to ensure status badges are contained in their own cells. A sidebar shell with light/dark themes and a new typeface was introduced. Submit buttons now have progress indicators and are protected from multiple submissions. Errors display within the console interface, and target lists now summarize backup statuses with links to detailed operation status.

atApproval.title: feat(target): edit a target's connection details

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Editing a target's connection details is now supported.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: This feature was added to allow users to update connection information for an existing target.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: A new capability has been introduced to modify the connection details associated with a configured target. Specific method names, APIs, or configuration parameters are not detailed.

atApproval.title: feat(api): expose backup checksums (DBV-15, DBV-999)

neutralSummary.whatChanged: The API now exposes backup checksums, including the recorded checksum value and the algorithm used.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: Users need to verify the integrity of downloaded backup artifacts by comparing checksums.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: The backup resource in the API now includes fields for the checksum (e.g., SHA-256) and the algorithm. API responses are updated accordingly, with no breaking changes to existing structure.

atApproval.title: feat(restore): restore a backup into any registered target

neutralSummary.whatChanged: A new feature was added that allows backups to be restored into any registered target.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: This enables greater flexibility by allowing users to choose the destination for a restore operation.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: The restore process is enhanced to support specifying any registered target as the destination for a backup restore, rather than being limited to a default or original target.

atApproval.title: feat(history): page the backup and restore history

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Paging was added to the backup and restore history feature.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: To improve the usability and handling of large history datasets for backup and restore operations.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: The history for backup and restore operations now supports pagination, allowing users to view data in chunks rather than loading the entire history at once.

atApproval.title: feat(backup): delete backups in bulk and remove a target with its backups

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Bulk deletion of multiple backups and removal of a backup target together with its associated backups were added. The confirmation page totals files, bytes, and restore records before deletion. Pre-checks ensure that deletions are refused if a backup is running or being restored. Removing a target without backups keeps the one-click dialog; removing a target with backups requires confirmation and typing its name.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: This change improves usability and safety when managing backups, providing batch operations and stronger checks to prevent accidental disruption of active processes.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: Bulk operations check all items for running or restoring status before any deletion. A confirmation page summarizes the impact. Single backup deletion now blocks if the backup is being restored. Target removal with backups now requires user confirmation with the target's name.

atApproval.title: perf(restore): stream gunzip into the client (DBV-32)

neutralSummary.whatChanged: The restore process now streams gunzip output directly into the MySQL client rather than decompressing the archive to disk first.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: This change eliminates the need for free disk space equal to the size of the uncompressed archive, improving disk usage and efficiency during restores.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: Gunzip is executed in its own dedicated thread which feeds decompressed data to MySQL's stdin, also using dedicated threads for each pipe to prevent thread pool exhaustion. Truncated or failing sources terminate the client process promptly. This approach is elaborated in ADR-016.

atApproval.title: feat(engine): route backups by engine and add PostgreSQL (DBV-10)

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Database connection tests, backups, and restores are now routed based on the target database engine, with support added for PostgreSQL alongside existing MySQL functionality. PostgreSQL adapters, UI support, runtime handling, migration coverage, integration tests, and updated documentation are included. Restores are limited to the original engine type.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: To enable support for PostgreSQL databases and to ensure backups and restores are handled according to the engine type, preventing incompatibility issues.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: Routing logic determines the appropriate engine adapter (MySQL or PostgreSQL) for connection tests, backups, and restores. The code backfills existing targets as MySQL, restricts restores to the registered engine, and delivers necessary tests and docs. A registered target's engine cannot be changed post-registration.
neutralSummary.migrationStep: No specific migration required unless supporting PostgreSQL targets; the system restricts changes to a target's engine after registration.

atApproval.title: feat(schedule): Quartz backup schedules

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Added support for Quartz backup schedules.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: To provide enhanced scheduling capabilities for backups, as per specification DBV-12-quartz.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: The implementation introduces integration with Quartz for managing backup job schedules. Referenced spec is DBV-12-quartz, but technical specifics are limited in this summary.

atApproval.title: DBV-12: Backup schedules

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Backup scheduling for targets is now possible using cron expressions with a selected time zone.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: To allow operators to automate backups according to custom timetables and ensure reliability even after restarts or downtime.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: Schedules for backups are stored persistently so they survive restarts. If a scheduled backup run is missed due to downtime, it will be triggered once the server starts again.

atApproval.title: feat(retention): keep the newest N backups per target (DBV-13)

neutralSummary.whatChanged: A new retention feature was added to keep only the newest N successful backups per target.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: To control storage growth by limiting the number of backups retained and discarding older ones.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: Failed backups are excluded from the N count, and deletion of old backup artifacts is logged.
neutralSummary.migrationStep: Configure the retention setting to specify how many recent backups to keep, if desired. No other special migration needed.

atApproval.title: feat(storage): S3-compatible storage profiles (DBV-11)

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Added support for S3-compatible storage profiles, allowing artifacts to be stored in any S3-compatible bucket via named profiles.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: To give operators the flexibility to use different S3-compatible storage solutions (such as AWS S3 and MinIO) for artifact storage, and to enhance security by encrypting secret keys.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: The implementation supports multiple storage profiles, each referencing an S3-compatible endpoint with encrypted secret credentials. Profiles can be tested before use to ensure proper configuration.

atApproval.title: feat(cli)!: take the backup target as --target-id (DBV-17)

neutralSummary.whatChanged: The CLI now requires the backup target ID to be provided with the --target-id option instead of as a positional argument.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: Users were mistakenly passing the target's name instead of its ID as a positional argument, resulting in 'not found' errors. This change clarifies and enforces correct input.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: The previous positional argument for target ID in 'dbvault backups' has been replaced with an explicit --target-id flag. Using the old form results in a usage error with exit code 2.
neutralSummary.migrationStep: Update any scripts or manual commands to use --target-id <id> instead of passing the target ID positionally.

atApproval.title: fix: honour DBVAULT_URL environment variable (DBV-18)

neutralSummary.whatChanged: The CLI now correctly prioritizes the DBVAULT_URL environment variable over the configuration file when determining which server to connect to.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: Previously, the CLI ignored the DBVAULT_URL variable, always using the server address from the config file even when the environment variable was set. This fix ensures expected environment variable precedence.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: DBVAULT_URL now takes precedence; if it's set, its value is used as the server address. If not, the CLI uses the address from ~/.config/dbvault/cli.properties, and if neither is set, it defaults to http://localhost:8090.

atApproval.title: fix(backup): unique local artifact paths per execution (DBV-14)

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Local backup artifacts now use unique file paths for each backup execution to prevent collisions when multiple backups run at the same time for the same database.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: Previously, two backups initiated in the same second for the same database could overwrite each other's files, causing data loss.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: Artifacts are now stored in the format BACKUP_DIR/<target-id>/<execution-id>/<file>, matching existing remote key structures. The backup process now refuses to run if the local destination already exists, and it cleans up empty directories left behind after deletes. Legacy flat artifacts continue to be accessible.

atApproval.title: fix(crypto): derive per-target keys with HKDF (DBV-16)

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Encryption of each target's password now uses a unique key derived from the master key via HKDF with the target's ID as context, instead of encrypting all passwords with the same key.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: To prevent a security vulnerability where leaking one master key and any ciphertext exposed all targets' credentials (DBV-16).
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: A new HKDF-SHA256 implementation derives per-target encryption keys. Old passwords decrypt as before and migrate to per-target keys on their next edit, while new passwords use the new format marked with a 'v2:' prefix. The master key or any per-target key alone can no longer decrypt all targets' credentials. `EncryptionPort` now provides 'encryptFor' and 'decryptFor', and all relevant flows use these methods.
neutralSummary.migrationStep: No direct action is required; credentials migrate to the new key scheme individually on update.

atApproval.title: Security review of credential encryption

neutralSummary.whatChanged: A review was conducted on dbvault's credential encryption, covering encryption key management and exposure risks from database dumps.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: To assess the security posture and identify areas for future improvement, with findings documented for the Hardening epic.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: The review examined master key handling, key derivation, nonce reuse, and what can be leaked if only a database dump is obtained, but did not include code changes.

atApproval.title: test: PostgreSQL Testcontainers round trip

neutralSummary.whatChanged: The PostgreSQL Testcontainers integration test now covers a wider range of data types (`jsonb`, `timestamptz`, `bytea`, `numeric`), as well as an index, view, foreign key, and bigserial sequence continuation checks.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: To make the test suite better reflect real-world database schemas and prevent regressions in these additional PostgreSQL features.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: The test now round-trips data using more PostgreSQL data types and objects, and checks proper sequence advancement for bigserial columns after a restore. The PostgreSQL version used in tests matches the installed `pg_dump`. No production code is changed.

atApproval.title: Enable Dependabot alerts and version updates for dbvault

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Dependabot alerts and automated version update configuration were enabled for the dbvault repository.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: This was done to improve dependency management and keep the codebase up to date with security and compatibility fixes.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: A dependabot.yml file was added to configure weekly updates for Maven dependencies and GitHub Actions workflows, all targeting the develop branch.

atApproval.title: feat: document S3 storage profiles

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Added documentation on configuring S3-compatible storage profiles for backups, including setup steps and policy requirements.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: To guide users on configuring and managing object storage profiles for backups and restores.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: The documentation explains setting up S3-compatible storage profiles (AWS S3 or MinIO), details each configuration field, outlines required bucket policies, describes backup/restore interactions with the staging directory, and clarifies which settings may or may not be changed after backups exist.

atApproval.title: DBV-19: Document S3-compatible storage for customers

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Added documentation guiding S3-compatible storage usage, detailing supported providers and required bucket permissions for dbvault.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: Customers requested clarity on which S3-compatible storage providers are supported and the necessary bucket permissions for dbvault operation.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: The new guide covers AWS S3 and MinIO, including an example of a minimal bucket policy required for access. No changes were made to application code or configuration—only documentation was updated.

atApproval.title: fix

neutralSummary.whatChanged: The console now shows backup sizes in B, KB, MB, GB, or TB instead of a raw byte count.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: Sizes are formatted on the Backups list, a backup's page, and the delete confirmations. A new ByteSizes helper formats them for the console templates: below 1024 bytes the exact count (1023 B); from 1024 bytes up, units of 1024 with one decimal (1024 bytes is 1.0 KB, 61,301,298 bytes is 58.5 MB). A missing size still shows —. On a backup's page, the size's tooltip gives the exact byte count.

atApproval.title: refactor(adapters): extract a shared ClientBinaries check

neutralSummary.whatChanged: The startup client binary checks for MySQL and PostgreSQL were refactored into a shared check called ClientBinaries.require, and a small unit test was added for this component.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: This was done to avoid code duplication and simplify maintaining checks for client binaries across different database engines.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: Previously, MysqlBinaries and PostgresBinaries duplicated logic for ensuring required client binaries were available; now, both engines use a single ClientBinaries.require method. The existing adapters no longer contain duplicated code, and tests now directly cover the shared logic.

atApproval.title: ci: rotate S3 credentials used by integration tests

neutralSummary.whatChanged: S3 integration tests no longer contain hard-coded credentials; test credentials are now injected via repository secrets or generated randomly during local runs, and the S3 emulator image is pinned by digest.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: To prevent credential leaks and ensure tests do not pass with invalid or stale credentials, improving security and reliability in CI and local development.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: Repository secrets S3_TEST_ACCESS_KEY and S3_TEST_SECRET_KEY are used by the CI workflow. Locally, tests auto-generate credentials if none are provided. The emulator Docker image is referenced by digest, avoiding ambiguous updates from a tag.

atApproval.title: Rotate S3 credentials used by integration tests

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Integration tests no longer carry hard-coded S3 access credentials in the source; instead, credentials are injected via repository secrets for CI, or randomly generated for local runs. The S3 emulator image is now pinned by digest rather than by tag.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: This change prevents leaked or misused S3 credentials during testing, improves test security, and ensures that tests do not rely on shared, static credentials.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: Repository secrets S3_TEST_ACCESS_KEY and S3_TEST_SECRET_KEY are provided to the verify workflow for S3 integration tests. If these are not set (e.g., local development), each test run generates a new set of random credentials. Tests use an S3 emulator image that is now referenced by a fixed digest to avoid unintentional updates from a moving tag.
